A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same pattern-based concept activation vector research despite the changed title and substantial revision. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original toy experiments, MNIST/CIFAR10 model-correction results, and ImageNet/ISIC2019 artifact analyses, with additional experiments in Appendices C and D.

after.justification: V2 reports original concept-alignment, TCAV, and model-correction experiments on Bone Age, ISIC2019, and FunnyBirds, including extensive appendix results.

M1.justification: The CAV estimator remains covariance divided by label variance (v1 Equation 1; v2 Equation 3). However, its model-correction integration changes substantially: v1 uses A-ClArC augmentation or P-ClArC projection, whereas v2 adopts the cited RR-ClArC procedure with a squared directional-gradient training penalty (Section 4.3.2). This changes the correction objective and procedure without introducing a different pattern estimator.

E1.justification: V2 removes the MNIST/CIFAR10 experiments, explicit backdoor scenarios, and ILSVRC2012 artifact evaluations. It adds Bone Age brightness artifacts, controlled ISIC2019 timestamps, and FunnyBirds concept tasks. Real ISIC2019 band-aid evaluation remains and expands to rulers and skin markers. ImageNet remains a pretraining source rather than an artifact-evaluation benchmark.

E2.justification: V1 primarily compares pattern-CAVs with SVM-derived CAVs and baseline models. V2 systematically evaluates lasso, logistic regression, ridge regression, and SVM CAVs alongside pattern-CAVs, retaining a vanilla model control for correction. Its TCAV comparison additionally includes sample-specific ground-truth directions (Figure 6).

E3.justification: V2 replaces the small-CNN controlled experiments with VGG16, ResNet18, and EfficientNet-B0 evaluations and examines many more layers. It introduces paired-sample cosine alignment, AUC, TCAV, and artifact-relevance metrics, plus mask-based insertion of real artifacts into test images. Its correction experiments use ten-epoch RR-ClArC training and validation-selected penalty weights, unlike v1's five-epoch augmentation or training-free projection.

E4.justification: V2 extends the distractor demonstration with feature-scaling, noise-magnitude, and random-seed experiments, and adds preprocessing sensitivity, layerwise correction, neuron-visualization, and TCAV-localization analyses. V1's predicted-versus-ground-truth artifact-label study (Appendix C), fine-tuning trajectories, and ImageNet nearest-neighbor case studies are removed rather than relocated.

E5.justification: V1 provides averaged results and shaded curves in Figure 4 without defining their uncertainty calculation. V2 explicitly reports standard errors for alignment/AUC and correction results, specifies Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney-based AUC error estimation, and adds seed-varying toy examples. These additions establish expanded uncertainty reporting, not an increase in repeated model-training runs.

E6.justification: Most result sets are replaced or newly introduced. For example, v1 Table 1 reports poisoned CIFAR10-box input accuracy of 0.730 versus 0.625 for pattern versus filter A-ClArC; v2 Table 1 reports 0.69 versus 0.36 for pattern versus SVM RR-ClArC on controlled ISIC2019 with VGG16. These are different settings, not cross-version performance gains. V2 additionally reports alignment, separability, and TCAV outcomes.

T1.justification: V1 supplies the covariance estimator, correction equations, and a toy signal/distractor construction. V2 adds substantial mathematical analysis in Appendix A: the binary-label difference-of-means derivation, coordinate-scaling behavior, expected robustness to independent zero-mean noise, and logistic/SVM divergence arguments, including Theorems A.1–A.3.

C1.justification: V1 centers its contributions on PatClArC and removal of Clever Hans and backdoor behavior. V2 reframes the central contribution around directional precision versus concept separability and adds a main claim about improving TCAV sensitivity testing. The claim that pattern-based vectors better estimate concept directions remains, while the specific backdoor-removal contribution disappears.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive applicability qualifications: filter-CAVs may be preferable for concept detection and bottleneck models, estimated artifact masks can distort evaluation, and correlated signals may explain the Bone Age exception. It also interprets ResNet18's spatially diffuse TCAV maps. V1 instead emphasizes MNIST backdoor failures and the limitation of representing artifacts with one linear direction.

D1.justification: V1 documents MNIST colors, a small CNN, and its AdaDelta schedule. V2 provides substantially fuller information for its experiments: dataset counts and splits, FunnyBirds class construction, pretrained-weight provenance, optimizer/learning-rate/epoch schedules, and the RR-ClArC penalty search and selected values (Appendices B and C.4; Tables 2–5). It also identifies the attribution software and configuration.

R1.justification: V2 retains the foundational Haufe, Kindermans, TCAV, and ClArC references but substantially redirects related work from broad explainability and backdoor defenses toward concept representations and applications. Added positioning includes superposition, CRAFT, concept activation regions, post-hoc concept bottlenecks, and RR-ClArC, rather than merely updated bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. PCAV/PatClArC terminology gives way to pattern-CAV terminology, and the experimental narrative is reorganized around directional accuracy and downstream applications. The appendices are rebuilt around methods/proofs, experimental details, and additional results.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout and substantially redesigns the visual presentation. New introductory concept illustrations, alignment plots, sensitivity maps, and grouped multi-metric tables replace much of v1's correction tables and nearest-neighbor galleries. Attribution-difference displays also change their organization and color conventions; this exceeds renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the central concept-direction claim by replacing largely indirect validation with paired-sample alignment measurements, broader comparisons, and explicit mathematical analysis. Fuller protocol documentation and uncertainty reporting also improve assessability. These gains outweigh the loss of earlier backdoor and predicted-label studies, although v2 introduces reporting problems: some band-aid values disagree between Tables 1 and 7, and Section 4.3.1 equates zero sensitivity with TCAV 0.5 despite Equation 6's strict-positive definition.
